blocks.text: 1. R-CNN

blocks.alt: An input image produces region proposals, each run through a CNN, then classified and regressed

blocks.text: OCR, the final topic of the previous Computer Vision Tasks module, closed out coverage of what these tasks actually accomplish. R-CNN opens the Object Detection Models module as one of the earliest influential approaches to actually implementing Object Detection.
Region-based Convolutional Neural Network works by proposing regions, then classifying each one, a genuinely two-stage strategy explored throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Task Being Solved
This connects back to Object Detection, already covered in its own topic. Object Detection genuinely needs both bounding boxes and class labels, already covered there as its own two-part output.
R-CNN genuinely tackles this with a two-stage pipeline, covered throughout the rest of this topic, one of the genuinely earliest concrete architectures built specifically to solve that exact task.
3. The Region Proposal Stage

blocks.alt: Selective search on an image produces about 2000 region proposals

blocks.text: The genuinely first stage uses a genuinely separate algorithm that proposes several thousand candidate regions that might contain an object, before any deep learning happens at all.

These candidate regions genuinely come before any Convolutional Neural Network gets involved at all, a genuinely distinct, separate step from the classification stage covered in the very next section.

blocks.text: 4. Per-Region Classification

blocks.alt: Each region proposal goes through CNN feature extraction to a class label

blocks.text: This connects back to Image Classification, already covered in its own topic. Each genuinely individual candidate region gets cropped out and run through a separate Image Classification network.
This is exactly the classification task already covered there, just applied to genuinely many small regions instead of one whole image, repeated once for every single proposed region.
5. Bounding Box Regression

blocks.alt: A rough proposal box is refined by bounding box regression

blocks.text: This connects back to the bounding box concept, already covered in Object Detection. A genuinely separate regression step refines each region's own rough box into a genuinely tighter, more accurate one.
This produces the genuinely final, precise bounding box already covered as Object Detection's own output format, correcting the rough, initial proposal already covered as the region proposal stage.
6. The Speed Problem

A genuinely severe, real practical problem connects back to per-region classification, already covered in this topic. Running a genuinely full Convolutional Neural Network separately on thousands of regions per image is genuinely extremely slow.

This genuinely severe slowness, already covered in this section, is R-CNN's own most significant, real practical limitation, motivating every architectural improvement covered in the rest of this module.

blocks.title: warning
blocks.content: This speed problem, already covered in this topic, made R-CNN genuinely impractical for many real-time applications, directly motivating the faster architectures covered in the very next two topics of this module.

blocks.text: 7. Redundant Computation

blocks.alt: Each region gets its own separate CNN pass, causing redundant computation

blocks.text: This connects back to Feature Maps, already covered in the CNN module. Many candidate regions genuinely overlap heavily with each other, already covered as a natural consequence of the region proposal stage.

This means recomputing genuinely similar features again and again for each overlapping region, a genuinely wasteful redundancy that compounds directly with the speed problem already covered in the previous section.
8. A Genuine Historical Contribution

A genuinely important historical contribution connects back to AlexNet, already covered in the CNN Architectures module. R-CNN genuinely demonstrated that deep Convolutional Neural Networks could dramatically outperform prior Object Detection approaches.

This directly extended AlexNet's own genuinely dramatic success in Image Classification, already covered, into the genuinely harder, richer task of Object Detection, already covered throughout this topic.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing Why R-CNN Is Genuinely Still Worth Understanding

blocks.alt: Wanting to understand detection history points toward studying R-CNN

blocks.text: This connects back to the two-stage design pattern, already covered in this topic. This exact pattern, propose then classify, genuinely underlies several later, faster architectures covered in this module.

Genuinely understanding the speed problem, already covered, motivates every improvement covered in the following two topics. Fast R-CNN and Faster R-CNN, both covered next, directly address this exact bottleneck.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates R-CNN's own conceptual pipeline in code, illustrating the region proposal and per-region classification stages already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)

# Stage 1: region proposals, already covered in this topic (using random boxes as a stand-in)
num_proposals = 5
proposals = [(rng.randint(0, 50), rng.randint(0, 50), rng.randint(100, 200), rng.randint(100, 200)) for _ in range(num_proposals)]

def classify_region(region_box, rng):
    # a genuinely simplified stand-in for running a full Image Classification network, already covered in this topic
    classes = ["background", "car", "person", "dog"]
    return rng.choice(classes), rng.uniform(0.5, 0.99)

print(f"Stage 1: {num_proposals} region proposals generated (already covered in this topic)")
print("\nStage 2: per-region classification (already covered in this topic):")
for i, box in enumerate(proposals):
    predicted_class, confidence = classify_region(box, rng)
    print(f"  Region {i + 1} at {box}: predicted '{predicted_class}' with confidence {confidence:.2f}")

print(f"\nNotice: {num_proposals} genuinely separate classification runs were needed for just this one image, already covered as the speed problem in this topic")

blocks.content: Running this example shows a genuinely separate classification call for every single proposed region, exactly the speed problem already covered in this topic, since real R-CNN implementations propose thousands of regions per image, not just five.

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: R-CNN, Region-based Convolutional Neural Network, proposes regions, then classifies each one.
It uses a genuinely separate algorithm to propose thousands of candidate regions first.
Each candidate region gets cropped out and classified independently.
A separate bounding box regression step refines rough proposals into tighter, more accurate boxes.
Running a full network separately on thousands of regions per image is genuinely extremely slow.
Heavily overlapping regions lead to genuinely wasteful, redundant feature computation.
R-CNN demonstrated that deep Convolutional Neural Networks could dramatically outperform prior detection approaches.
Its propose-then-classify pattern underlies several later, faster architectures covered in this module.
Next up: Fast R-CNN, which directly addresses R-CNN's own speed problem.
